title: Apple: It Was Never About an iPhone Super Cycle, Says Guggenheim

https://www.barrons.com/articles/apple-it-was-never-about-an-iphone-super-cycle-says-guggenheim-1517366458 Apple: It Was Never About an iPhone Super Cycle, Says Guggenheim By Jan. 30, 2018 9:40 p.m. ET Text Size Medium Large 
As more and more Street observers wring their hands over what they conjecture could be a short-fall in Apple 's ( AAPL ) March-quarter iPhone sales — Deutsche Bank today said you should give up on the fantasy of a “super cycle” — some are distancing themselves from the expectation of big iPhone numbers. 
In this form of analyst jujitsu, Guggenheim analyst Robert Cihra this evening reiterates a Buy rating on Apple, and a $215 price target, writing that the “supply chain negativity looks like a buying opportunity to us,” and that “singular new iPhone X SKU” is "starting a MULTI-year upgrade cycle (e.g., to OLED screens, 3D sensing/Face ID using on-device ML, AR) and NOT some big 1-year 'super-cycle’." 
A slower growth outlook for Apple is good, he writes: 
We have repeatedly laid out that we do NOT see Apple’s new iPhone X setting up some one-year “super-cycle” but rather that it represents a new high-end SKU with NEW TECHNOLOGIES that can drive an elongated MULTI-year upgrade cycle as OLED, 3D cameras, on-device ML, and augmented reality/ AR features waterfall into mainstream models over the coming 1-3 years. Ultimately, we continue to think that is an even better scenario for AAPL stock since a 1-year jump would have driven fears of a subsequent cliff, whereas we are currently estimating that after iPhone units grow +6%Y/Y in CY18E they can grow another +4%Y/Y in CY19E. 
The real thing is the average selling price , contends Cihra, not the volume of iPhones sold. 
And so, he cuts his own estimates for fiscal 2018 “way back” to just 3% growth from 2017 versus what he had thought would be 13% growth. 
There are “enough negative supply-chain data points” piling up, he writes, including Corning 's ( GLW ) report yesterday morning, in which it pointed to a 30% drop in its sales of Gorilla Glass for smartphones because of an expected "low-single digit smartphone market unit growth." 
"HOWEVER, we have long projected higher blended ASPs being the much bigger driver,” writes Cihra. 
With higher average selling prices this year — he models iPhone ASP of $758 in 2018, up from $662 last year — 2018’s revenue can rise by 15% versus 10% last year, to $270 million. That’s down from his original $287 billion, and just below consensus for $271 billion. 
Moreover, Apple’s EPS should get to $13 this calendar year, and $14 in calendar 2019, which gives the stock a 10 times P/E , after backing out cash. Most Popular
